question.text: A vehicle travels horizontally along a direct path at a steady speed of 30 ms⁻¹. An object is launched straight up from this vehicle so that it lands back at its exact launching spot after the vehicle has traveled a distance of 80 m. What is the required launch speed with respect to the vehicle? (Use g = 10 ms⁻²)
conditions: cart moves horizontally at constant speed 30 ms⁻¹
particle projected vertically upwards relative to the cart
particle lands back at its launch point on the cart after the cart travels 80 m

solution.approach: Find the time of flight from the cart's speed and distance moved, then use it as the projectile's up-and-down time to find launch speed relative to the cart.

steps.text: The cart moves at constant speed 30 ms⁻¹ and covers 80 m while the projectile is in the air. Find the time of flight.
Relative to the cart, the projectile only moves vertically: straight up and back down to the same point on the cart. This is the usual vertical time of flight.
Solve for the vertical launch speed relative to the cart.
